newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee retreats from high, fund buying ebbs.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee retreats from high, fund buying ebbs.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures stepped back from the session peaks to end Monday with pared gains as fund and trade buying fizzled out in the afternoon.
Traders said the market lost the upward momentum as roller-coaster New York-listed arabicas headed south after May hit new contract highs of 224 cents a lb.
While robustas were seen as a bit toppish, market operators continued to lack the conviction to sell due to the jitters in New York.
New York rallied on Monday on fresh supply worries and news of the Colombian truck drivers' strike. But the market later pulled back, dented by fund profit-taking.
By 1628 GMT, New York's May traded 3.05 cents down at 213.50.
However, players in London remained wary with New York's May entering the first notice period on Tuesday. Deliverable coffee remained relatively small against the large open positions on May.
By the close, London's May was just $1 higher at $1,641 a tonne after a peak of $1,675, the highest level since March 26.
One trader said he would not be surprised if $1,675 would be the top of this week's trading.
Most-active July was $8 firmer at $1,670 after failing to stay above the $1,700 resistance.
Volume reached 5,609 lots. The May/July switch was again active, with some 800 lots changing hands at between $21-$28.
The Colombian strike had little influence in London. One trader said that a lot of coffee cargoes could have been rushed to the ports ahead of the strike.
Some also thought that the new strike was likely to be less disruptive than the crippling stoppage in January.
But broker GNI said around 200,000 to 350,000 bags of April shipments were still to be loaded.
It said while the government had threatened to declare the strike illegal, this did not stop the worker action in January.
In other stories, Brazil trade house Tristao put Brazil 1996/97 crop estimate at 27.5 million bags, up from its previous forecast of 25.85 million.
It pegged the 1997/98 crop at 23.5 million bags. It said the drop in output was partly cyclical in nature. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
